title: Backend entry domain sql joins indexes
topic: Backend entry domain sql joins indexes
question: Explain the difference between an INNER JOIN and a LEFT JOIN, and explain what a database index actually does to speed up a query.
idealAnswer:
INNER JOIN returns only rows where the join condition matches in both tables, LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table plus matched rows from the right, with NULLs filling in where there's no match

Gives a concrete scenario where the difference matters, e.g. listing all users including ones with zero orders requires LEFT JOIN, INNER JOIN would silently drop them

Explains an index as a separate, ordered data structure (commonly a B-tree) that lets the database find matching rows without scanning the whole table

Connects indexes to the columns used in WHERE, JOIN, and ORDER BY clauses, an index only helps if the query can actually use it

Mentions the tradeoff: indexes speed up reads but add overhead to writes (every insert/update/delete has to update the index too) and take up storage
